body.statement: For a finite ADMG and an ordinary interventional query, the success-or-failure decision of the ordinary \(\operatorname{ID}\) algorithm is computable in time polynomial in the graph encoding size.

source.locator: Section 2, pages 4--5, greedy valid-fixing-sequence decision without backtracking
source.verbatim_statement: While it might appear that checking whether elements of a set \(\vec{J}\) admit a valid sequence in \({\cal G}(\vec{V})\), and finding such a sequence, if it exists, might be a computationally challenging problem, in fact this problem admits a low order polynomial time algorithm. This is because the fixing operator applied to graphs only removes edges and never adds edges. Removing an edge can never prevent a vertex from being fixable if it was fixable before the edge was removed. As a result, an algorithm looking for a valid sequence never needs to backtrack – finding any fixable vertex among vertices yet to be fixed suffices to eventually yield a fixing sequence if it exists, while being unable to find such a vertex at some point implies such a sequence does not exist.

attestation.note: Literal primary-source transcription from arXiv:2307.03750v1 HTML, Section 2, accessed 2026-09-13.

body.justification: Polynomial graphical ID decision is the verifier needed for membership of the realization count in \(\#\mathrm P\).
